title: [recoverability] backup.rs signs correctly with curl 7.88 and newer: the payload hash on every request, both listings' query in SigV4's sorted order
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 136 [recoverability]: `spawn backup` and `spawn store` sign their R2 requests correctly with curl 7.88 and newer. 7.88 is Debian 12's curl, and the likely second host (D1) runs Debian 12. This takes PR #59's change in through the gate (lead-mac's decision of 2026-11-13 23:03). The contract is ours. Where things stand (main d3cb43b9; crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs): - Every bucket request is one curl call. Spawn hands curl a config on stdin (`bucket_request`): credentials, `aws-sigv4 = "aws:amz:auto:s3"`, the URL and the call's own headers. curl signs the request with SigV4. - No request names its payload hash (`x-amz-content-sha256`). R2 requires it on an s3 request. curl 8.5 (this host's) adds it itself; 7.88 does not, so every request from a 7.88 host fails. - SigV4 signs the query with its parameters sorted by name. A curl that signs the query as written (7.88) signs what the bucket checks only when it is already sorted. Two listings send a later page's query unsorted: - `list_bucket` (the whole bucket, before each dump and bundle: `?list-type=2&max-keys=1000&continuation-token=…`); - `list_prefix` (the store's manifests and segments: `?list-type=2&max-keys=1000&prefix=…&continuation-token=…`). Their first pages are sorted. A bucket of more than 1000 keys has a later page, so a 7.88 host's backup fails there. - deploy/backup/lib.sh's `s3()` (pg-backup.sh, the restore drill) has the same missing header. deploy/ is protected, so that one line is the owner's part (below), not this objective's code. Read: crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs (`bucket_request`, `list_bucket`, `list_prefix`, `put_new_object`, `percent_encode`), rsi/scenarios/116.sh (the world and 104's R2 stand-in). Required behaviour. - Every bucket request's curl config carries `header = "x-amz-content-sha256: UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD"`, next to the aws-sigv4 line and before the call's own headers. A curl that adds the header itself takes this one. - UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD: an upload is streamed and never read twice to hash it. R2 and S3 accept it for GET, HEAD, ListObjectsV2 and PUT, a conditional PUT (`If-None-Match: *`, put_new_object) included. - Both listings build their query in one function, with the parameters sorted by name: `?continuation-token=&list-type=2&max-keys=1000[&prefix=

]`, the token only on a later page. Values stay percent-encoded as today (`percent_encode`, SigV4's encoding). - Nothing else changes: - the credentials stay on curl's stdin, never argv; - every other request and verb is unchanged; - no record changes. - The owner's part (deploy/ is protected; sync/obj-136/deploy-136.diff, +8 lines, pushed by the lead with this contract): - lib.sh's `s3()` gains `-H "x-amz-content-sha256: UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD"`; - deploy/backup/README.md names the oldest curl (7.88, Debian 12's) and why, and its by-hand restore commands gain the same header. Unit tests (spawn-cli, backup.rs): - both listings, first page and later, with and without a prefix: the SigV4 canonical request built from the URL as sent has its query unchanged by sorting (continuation-token first), and the config's x-amz-content-sha256 header is signed with UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD as the payload hash; - every bucket request's config (a GET, a HEAD and a conditional PUT) names x-amz-content-sha256: UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, and no credential is in a header. Each rule removed alone must fail a test or the scenario. No test is renamed or dropped. Files (expected; no other open objective touches them): crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs only. The throwaway is +198 −27 in backup.rs: +49 −27 of code and doc comments (the config built in one function, the listings' query in one, the header constant), +149 of tests. The owner's deploy-136.diff touches deploy/backup/lib.sh (+1) and deploy/backup/README.md (+7). Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/136.sh. Black box on 116's world: its own database, scratch HOME, GNUPGHOME and key directory, and made-up keys and R2 credentials. - It runs against 104's local R2 stand-in, made strict as R2 is: - a request without x-amz-content-sha256 is 400; - a PUT with If-None-Match: * over an existing key is 412; - it still verifies every SigV4 signature, signed headers and payload hash (UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD) included; - it pages listings at 4 keys and logs each listing's parameter names in the order sent. - A `curl` first on PATH logs, for each call, the names of the headers Spawn's config gives it, and of any `-H` on its argv. It logs names only, never a value and never the user line, to a log under WORK, mode 600. Then it runs the real curl with the same config. (1) `spawn store put` six times under one prefix, then `spawn store list`: each exits 0, a manifest listing goes past its first page, and every listing sends its parameters sorted by name. (2) `spawn backup dump` with five other objects in the bucket: exits 0; the whole-bucket listing goes past its first page, sorted likewise. (3) Every curl call names x-amz-content-sha256, the conditional PUTs too, and none is refused. (5) deploy/backup/lib.sh, sourced from the tree under test as pg-backup.sh sources it: `list_objects` against the strict stand-in exits 0, names the dump's object, and its curl call names the header. (4) No secret in any output, record or the curl log. On main d3cb43b9 (through the gate's harness, curl 8.5), 136.sh exits 1 at its first failed check: "(1) store listings send their parameters out of SigV4's sorted order: list-type,max-keys,prefix,continuation-token". Each check stops the run (116's harness). - On this host the base's requests are not refused: curl 8.5 sends x-amz-content-sha256 itself. So check (3) reads the config Spawn hands curl, not the wire. With only the header removed (mutant header-dropped), 136.sh fails "(3) 76 of 76 curl call(s) name no x-amz-content-sha256 header". - The other mutants, each alone: token-last (both listings) fails (1) and a unit test; bucket-token-last fails (2); prefix-token-last fails (1). - On the throwaway, 136.sh passes twice, and 104.sh, 114.sh and 116.sh pass. - clippy (-p spawn-cli, all targets, -D warnings) and fmt pass, and the backup tests pass (55). - The test list gains the 2 tests above, and none is missing. Verified by: the gate runs 136.sh on the candidate. After the landing, the lead runs one real read: `spawn store list` against spawn-work. It pages when the bucket holds more than a page, and reading its curl config is not needed: the header and the order are what this contract fixes. The PUT side is proven on the stand-in only: store puts stay off until A43/A44 and lead-mac's word. The lead posts the read's exit and its manifest count in sync. On a Debian 12 host (D1), when there is one, the first hourly dump is the 7.88 proof.
